independent_materiality.governance_proposition: Parallel agents do not by themselves establish collaboration or distributed constraint dissolution.

condition_tests.literal_condition: A materially consequential task or decision pathway is decomposed across multiple agents, sub-agents, tools, orchestration layers, roles, queues, or optimisation units.
condition_tests.assessment: Multiple runs exist, but a decomposed shared task graph is not established.

condition_tests.literal_condition: One or more higher-order identity, safety, ethical, dignity, welfare, care, continuity, or governance constraints apply to the aggregate task trajectory rather than only to one isolated local action.
condition_tests.assessment: General constraints may apply individually.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Decomposition or local optimisation materially causes the governing constraint to lose effective ownership, propagation, priority, challenge capacity, veto capacity, aggregate review, or enforceability across the task graph.
condition_tests.assessment: No causal loss of global ownership through decomposition is evidenced.

condition_tests.literal_condition: No effective component or orchestration layer retains and successfully exercises responsibility sufficient to detect, challenge, prevent, or correct the aggregate constraint failure before the material outcome or trajectory is produced.
condition_tests.assessment: Absence of a coordinating layer is not proof that one was required.

condition_tests.literal_condition: The aggregate trajectory violates or materially weakens the governing constraint even though one or more local components may have complied with or optimised their bounded roles.
condition_tests.assessment: No aggregate failure mechanism follows solely from parallel execution.

literal_exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Distributed execution preserves explicit global constraint ownership, propagation, cross-agent challenge or veto pathways, aggregate-outcome review, and traceability while permitting role-specialised local optimisation.

Not aligned exclusion: A genuine sub-agent or worker role lawfully narrows task scope, tool access, execution authority, or reporting responsibility while applicable higher-order constraints remain effective across the aggregate trajectory.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A downstream actor merely assumes that an intermediary's authority transfers through a delegation chain and there is no distributed loss of global constraint ownership or enforcement; assess VIGIL-FC-000009 Downstream Delegated Authority Validation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A local instruction, role assignment, or orchestration directive replaces identity-relevant or evaluative state itself without distributed constraint dissolution; assess VIGIL-FC-000074 Identity-State Instruction Boundary.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Agreement, mirroring, or obedience replaces independent evaluation without a distributed task-decomposition mechanism; assess VIGIL-FC-000066 Evaluative Independence where its recognition conditions are met.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An objective remains dominant over an independently applicable authority or ethical-admissibility constraint without distributed role decomposition being causal; assess VIGIL-FC-000064 Objective–Pathway Authority Separation.
Not aligned exclusion: A single component fails to apply a constraint that remained fully owned, propagated, and enforceable across the system; classify the component-level mechanism instead.
class_tests.operative_exclusion_assessment: Independent component activity is distinct from distributed causal dissolution; do not infer collusion from shared inputs.
class_tests.opposite_polarity_assessment: No demonstrated aggregate responsibility pathway supports a positive mapping.

independent_materiality.governance_proposition: An unrelated operational cluster can still exhibit a class-worthy AI-infrastructure occurrence.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Identifiable material serves an authentication or authorisation function, or contains the protected secret content needed to exercise that function, in an AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure.
condition_tests.assessment: Authentication material is stored in AI-operation panels.

condition_tests.literal_condition: An independently evidenced custody boundary governs who or what may hold, receive, disclose, modify or replace the material in the assessed lifecycle stage.
condition_tests.assessment: Secrets function as credentials rather than public connection labels.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Occurrence evidence demonstrates exposure outside that boundary, unauthorised acquisition, or unauthorised custody-changing modification or replacement. Demonstrated retrievability of protected secret content is sufficient without proof of subsequent credential use.
condition_tests.assessment: Publicly accessible panels expose that material outside the intended custody boundary.

literal_exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The material is only a non-secret identifier, public connection identifier, public verification key or public client configuration that is intended to be available in the assessed context. A separately exposed secret or unauthorised protected-information operation requires its own assessment.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue concerns only coherent propagation of expiry, revocation, refresh or replacement into sessions and dependent operations. Assess Authentication-State Continuity unless a separate custody property is evidenced.

Not aligned exclusion: Credential handling or delegation is validly authorised and preserves the applicable custody boundary. Mere credential possession or ordinary authorised use is not a custody defect.

Not aligned exclusion: Only a theoretical vulnerability, unverified secret classification, unusable placeholder or unsuccessful attempt is shown; protected authentication material is not demonstrated outside custody.
Not aligned exclusion: Material is already invalid and no residual secret-protection or custody obligation is independently established. Do not assume every expired token remains a usable secret.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The only property is the scope of an action performed using a credential, without a distinct custody issue. Assess the applicable authority or action class.
class_tests.operative_exclusion_assessment: Validity checking strengthens the custody concern; separate non-secret target information may engage FC089. Do not attribute all panels to AIA0001.
class_tests.opposite_polarity_assessment: No tested preservation of credential confidentiality is established.

rows.source_specific_reasoning: Reconsider FC090 failure for the broader exposed-panel occurrence, with an explicitly separate actor/scope from E003. 'Not all panels belong to this cluster' justifies attribution separation, not declaring the custody phenomenon non-classifiable.
rows.taxonomy_gap_assessment: Existing custody coverage suffices; no harness-secrets-specific class needed.
rows.outstanding_uncertainty: Individual owners, permission records and validity coverage not fully public.
rows.other_incident_implications: Compare exposed secrets in legitimate red-team and malicious harnesses; both need independently scoped custody review.

previous_decision_preservation.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A broader research disclosure cannot automatically be assigned as this bounded actor's distinct confidentiality impact.
